finding.text: `review/diff.patch` is the wrong diff — it contains the sibling task's changes (`part1b-inbox-restructure`: `core/Page/ext/Inbox/*`, `ai2/rail.js`, `ext/drawer/*`), not one line of `ext/panel2/`. Whoever generates this review artifact for part1-panel2 needs to re-run it against the actual Panel2 work; as it stands the review package doesn't let anyone check this task from the diff alone.

The real Panel2 work (`public/framework/ext/panel2/Panel2.js`, `panel2.css`, `page.js`, `readme.md`, `doc/`) is untracked in the worktree (`git status` shows `??` on the whole directory and on `.../part1-panel2/`) — nothing was committed despite the brief's "commit your work there as you go (small commits)" rule. Nothing is lost yet, but a repo crash or `git clean` before the next step would destroy it.

Judged from the actual files on disk (not the diff, since it's unusable — see #1): the module does what requirements.md asked. `Panel2.js` has header/main/footer + start/end sides as parts-as-statics (`Panel2.Header/.Main/.Footer/.Side`), a real toolbar container (`header.append()` lands in `.controls`, not a config array), `Panel2.split(a, b, { axis })` reusing `ext/grip` untouched, and `.panel2-grid` reusing `framework.css`'s existing `grid auto` formula rather than inventing one. `page.js` shows a plain panel, a live resizable split with real header buttons, the grid, and — better than the brief's "screenshot is acceptable for the phone case" — a genuinely live phone demo via a same-page `?view=phone` iframe instead of a screenshot. The two deferred items (fixed/fluid split, multi-grip) plus the two owner-added ones (Sprawl, adaptive split height) are each a short readme paragraph with why, as asked.

`readme.md` says the `panel2-` CSS prefix was confirmed free in `css-scopes.txt` but wasn't written there because that file is outside this task's fence — true per the brief, but worth someone actually adding the line soon so a second module doesn't grab `panel2-` first.
No simpler way stood out — the module is already small (one file, four static parts, one split function, one grid class), consistent with CLAUDE.md law 1.

A side only becomes a drawer when the whole browser window is narrow (`@media (width < 34em)`), not when the panel itself is narrow. So a Panel2 with a 16rem side, placed in a 22rem `.panel2-grid` cell on a wide screen, leaves main about 6rem wide (layout 3, layout 18) — panel2.css, the drawer rule. Part 2 builds a dashboard of these, so a container query is worth deciding before then.

The phone iframe loads the whole site shell (site header, Panel2 title, tabs) inside 22em × 26em, so the panel being shown is a small strip at the bottom. A white sliver from the closed drawer, probably its box-shadow, shows at the frame's left edge (layout 10, words 4) — my full-page headless shot at 1200, phone section.

The readme says two things the code doesn't do: its Architecture lists a `static grid` that doesn't exist, and it says the header's controls use flex-wrap, but `.panel2-controls` is plain `display: flex` with no wrap (words 7) — readme.md and panel2.css.

The drawer has a literal colour, `box-shadow: 0 0 1.5em rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`, and it has no backdrop. Tapping outside the drawer doesn't close it; only the header toggle does (colour 3) — panel2.css, the drawer rule.
The grid demo ends with Panel C alone on row 2 at the stage's 817px width (layout 11) — full-page shot at 1200, grid demo.

Some paragraphs run past 60 words: the page's phone-section intro (~75), the grid intro (~65), and the readme's Open questions items 3 and 4 (~90 each) (words 3). The readme's H1 is also a whole sentence where a name was wanted.
`panel2-` is still not reserved in `css-scopes.txt`. It is recorded in doc/decisions.md for someone who is allowed to edit that file.
This review's diff.patch also contains part1b (Inbox restructure) and ai2/drawer files. I reviewed only the ext/panel2 files, plus the one-line ext/page.js and ext/readme.md entries.
